messages:
Noah: Hi team, first day sprinting into issues — trying to switch to the AWS account for dev infra (role arn: arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/Redwood-Dev-Infra-Role) via Okta but getting 'AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole'. I followed the Okta > AWS app flow and picked the role. Anyone seen this before?
Chris (security): Welcome Noah! Two quick things: do you have MFA enabled in Okta? We enforce MFA for AssumeRole. Also check if your SSO session expired — try logging out of Okta and re-authing.
Noah: Yep MFA prompted during login. Re-auth'd; still same error. Tried CLI too: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/Redwood-Dev-Infra-Role --role-session-name noah-test` returns same AccessDenied.
Lena (identity): Hi — can you paste the full error (redact IDs) and confirm whether you're in the 'engineers' group in Okta? The AWS app maps groups to roles. If your Okta group isn't mapped, you'll see this.
Noah: Error: `An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the AssumeRole operation: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/Redwood-Dev-Infra-Role`
Noah: I'm listed in group `eng-infra`, but not sure if that's the exact mapping used.
Jamal (finance): Not sure it's finance-y, but FYI if the role has `iam:PassRole` restrictions tied to billing ops we sometimes lock it down. But sounds identity mapping.
Chris (security): Ok, @Lena can you check the Okta mapping for the AWS app? Also check if the role has an ExternalId or a Condition restricting SAML audience. Sometimes we require `aws:ViaAWSService` or SourceIdentity.
Lena (identity): Looking now. The AWS app mapping for `Redwood-Dev-Infra-Role` expects group `eng-devops` (not `eng-infra`). That explains it. I can add you to eng-devops for a week. Quick question: how long do you need access?
Noah: Just 5 days for onboarding and to provision a small test host and push some infra changes.
Lena (identity): Cool, I'll add you and re-push the app config. Give it ~5 minutes to propagate.
DevX Bot: Identity change queued: OKTA-3456 — Noah added to group eng-devops. Propagation ETA 300s.
Noah: Re-logged into Okta and tried the role again. Now I can assume role in console but CLI `aws sts assume-role` still fails the same way.
Chris (security): CLI often needs the SAML assertion or the Okta profile provider to exchange creds. Are you using the Okta AWS CLI helper or did you generate short-lived creds from the web console?
Noah: I'm using native AWS CLI with Okta helper (`okta-awscli`). I just ran `okta-awscli -p Redwood` and it printed creds but `aws sts get-caller-identity` shows my original org account, not assumed role.
Lena (identity): Run `okta-awscli -p Redwood --profile assumed` then `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile assumed`. Also check `~/.aws/config` for the `saml`/`source_profile` mapping.
Noah: Tried that; still not switching. Getting `ExpiredToken` sometimes but mostly AccessDenied.
Chris (security): Two more checks: 1) The role session duration may be limited (we have a 1h max). If the helper requests longer, AWS might reject. 2) The role trust policy might require `sts:ExternalId` matching Okta app. I'll ask infra to paste the role trust document.
Jamal (finance): Also note: billing console access is separate. Even if you get the infra role, you might not see Billing in the console unless you have `aws-portal` view permissions. If you need to check project billing, file a short request.
Lena (identity): I inspected the AWS app assertion; looks good. Chris, role trust has `Condition: {StringEquals: {sts:ExternalId: "okta-aws-2109"}}` — that matches our Okta app. Should be fine.
Chris (security): Hmm. Noah, can you try the web console to switch role via the role dropdown and then from the console click 'Switch Role' and create temporary creds (your browser session will be the assumed role)? If that works, it's an Okta-CLI mapping issue.
Noah: Web switch works now, I see the infra account and can view EC2. CLI still broken.
Lena (identity): For CLI, use the Okta session cookie exchange method: `okta-awscli --session-ttl 3600`. Also confirm you're running the latest `okta-awscli` and that `~/.okta/cache` isn't stale.
Noah: Updated okta-awscli to latest and cleared cache. Now `okta-awscli -p Redwood` gives me credentials and `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile assumed` returns the role arn. CLI works! Thanks.
Noah: One last thing: I still can't see the Cost Explorer in the account console. It says Access Denied on Billing. How do I request billing view?
Jamal (finance): Open a ticket in the billing queue (billing@redwood) with account id and role/user needing access. We'll grant `aws-portal:ViewBilling` or give you a Billing Console role for 7 days. Mention it's for onboarding.
Noah: Filed billing ticket BT-2026-78. Requesting 7d billing viewer for assumed role.
DevX Bot: Ticket BT-2026-78 created and assigned to Jamal (finance). ETA 2 business days.
Lena (identity): Great, glad CLI is unblocked. Noah, ping me if the Okta mapping behaves oddly later and we'll audit group sync.
Noah: Thanks everyone — huge help getting past SSO and CLI issues!
